'''Tony Lee Bradley Jr.''' (born January 8, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina]] (UNC). A 6'11 [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]], Bradley was a primary substitute for the Tar Heels' [[2016–17 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2017 NCAA championship team]].

Born and raised in [[Bartow, Florida]], Bradley played high school basketball for [[Bartow High School]]. He was named a [[McDonald's All-American]] in his senior year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Jordan|first1=Jason|title=Tony Bradley restores the 'Tar Heel order' in the McDonald's All American Game|url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/tony-bradley-restores-the-tar-heel-order-in-the-mcdonalds-all-american-game|accessdate=April 16, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|date=January 22, 2016}}</ref> Bradley chose North Carolina over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] and [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rankin|first1=Reggie|title=North Carolina opens 2016 class with five-star center Tony Bradley|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/13569012/five-star-center-recruit-tony-bradley-no-26-espn-100-2016-says-attend-north-carolina|accessdate=April 16, 2017|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=September 3, 2015}}</ref> In his freshman season, Bradley served as the primary reserve for senior [[Kennedy Meeks]], averaging 7.5 points and 5.1 rebounds in 14.6 minutes per game and providing strong offensive rebounding for the Tar Heels.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vecenie|first1=Sam|title=Tony Bradley is UNC's best pro prospect you haven't heard about — and he likes it that way|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/tony-bradley-unc-nba-draft-2017-north-carolina-basketball-final-four-scouting-report/5z6vdu1ac59b162nqyrovcxnv|accessdate=April 16, 2017|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=April 1, 2017}}</ref>

Following the Tar Heels' championship win over [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], Bradley announced that he would declare his eligibility for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without signing an agent, leaving open the opportunity to return to UNC for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=UNC's Bradley to test NBA draft waters after title win|url=http://collegebasketball.ap.org/article/uncs-bradley-test-nba-draft-waters-after-title-win|accessdate=April 16, 2017|work=collegebasketball.ap.org|date=April 4, 2017}}</ref>  Bradley ultimately chose to remain in the NBA Draft, becoming the third "one-and-done" player during Williams' tenure at UNC and the second among those to have won a national championship.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=UNC Basketball: Tony Bradley Jr. to stay in NBA Draft|url=http://keepingitheel.com/2017/05/24/unc-basketball-tony-bradley-jr-stay-nba-draft/|accessdate=June 20, 2017|work=Fansided|date=May 24, 2017}}</ref>
